newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche says banks to link, mergers not essential.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche says banks to link, mergers not essential.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG on Wednesday said German banks could work more closely together in future on various aspects of their business but would not necessarily have to merge.
Chief executive Rolf Breuer told the bank's interim news conference that back office operations links would likely pick up in the years to come.
"Legal fusion is not a precondition for this," he said.
"I can see the possibilities for more co-operation and we will see that increasing in years to come."
Breuer said various processing and pricing systems might be co-ordinated.
"Why for example must we prepare for the Euro separately and indeed in competition?," he asked.
The launch of the euro as planned in 1999 would increase competitive pressures on German banks, Breuer said.
"In 1999 the competition will really get going. And then the question is, who can survive? It will divide the big from the small, the fast from the slow and the industrious from the lazy."
